name: Kovalam Reef (Lighthouse Beach)
shape_type_notes: As-built structure appears to be an echelon/fan array of individual ~30 m geotextile bag units radiating from a focus near the rocky headland, producing a stepped/zigzag breaking line — NOT a single smooth curved crescent or delta wedge. Based on two independent photographic sources (S1/S2 ASR Ltd's own construction-phase aerial photo, and S3 Raised Water Research's traced wave-break outline). Medium confidence on typology; the exact number/angles of units is a schematic reconstruction (low confidence).
coords: metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid (approximated at the base of the rocky headland/‘Lighthouse Point’ immediately updrift of the reef); x = alongshore, positive toward the southeast (from the headland toward the main Lighthouse Beach hotel frontage, matching the sense of ASR Ltd's own construction-phase aerial photo, S2) — the true compass bearing of this alongshore direction was not found in any source and this sense is inferred from photo geometry only; y = offshore, positive seaward; shoreline approximated as the line y=0
polygon_notes: SCHEMATIC RECONSTRUCTION, not an as-built survey polygon — no engineering drawing or GPS as-built survey of the Kovalam reef was found in any source (ours or Gemini's). Constructed as three ~30 m geotextile-tube units (matching the sourced '30 m units' fact, R1/R2/R10) chained in a staggered/echelon 'staircase' with a 12 m tube width (width itself not sourced for Kovalam; borrowed by analogy from comparable ASR Ltd geobag reef crest widths, e.g. Gold Coast/Mt Maunganui-family designs, and from Gemini's own unsourced 12 m crest-width assumption, which is plausible but likewise unverified). Verified closed and non-self-intersecting with shapely (is_valid=True, is_simple=True, first vertex == last vertex).
area_m2_notes: This is the footprint of the geobag tubes themselves (slender fan, ~12 m wide), not a filled solid wedge — substantially smaller than Gemini's candidate (3,800 m² gross / 2,245 m² by their own polygon-area audit) because we model the structure as an open fan of narrow tubes, consistent with the photographic evidence in S2, rather than a solid crescent/delta mass. Low confidence — order-of-magnitude estimate only.

crest_depth_m.notes: No source (ours, Gemini's cited sources, or this pass's independent search) states a crest/submergence depth for the as-built Kovalam reef. Gemini's 1.6 m value traces to two citations ('Kerala Harbour Engineering Dept Project Report 2011' and 'Thomas et al. 2012 Performance Assessment of Kovalam Multipurpose Reef') that could not be located or confirmed to exist under those titles/years in this pass's search (see gemini_comparison). By loose analogy, comparable ASR Ltd geotextile multi-purpose reefs (Mount Maunganui, Narrowneck) sit roughly 1.5–2.5 m below chart datum, but this is a generic analogy, not a Kovalam-specific figure, and is not asserted as fact.

distance_offshore_m.notes: Not published in any source. Our schematic polygon's inner edge sits ~34 m and outer edge ~76 m from the shoreline baseline (centroid ~55 m); this range is a low-confidence visual impression from the ASR Ltd construction-phase aerial photo (S2), where swimmers/snorkellers are shown very close to both the shore and the reef, suggesting a near-shore siting broadly compatible with, but not confirming, Gemini's specific 150 m figure. Gemini's 150 m could not be verified against any accessible source either.

orientation_notes: The unit fan appears to originate from a focus close to the rocky headland ('Eve's/Lighthouse Point' area) immediately updrift of Lighthouse Beach, with the geotextile-tube units fanning alongshore toward the main hotel-fronted beach and outward to sea (per S2's aerial photo, where a labelled 'Reef' shows several dark parallel/sub-parallel submerged tube-rows radiating from near the point). No compass bearing for the arms, the shoreline, or the incident swell was found specifically sourced for Kovalam; Gemini's swell-direction figure (200–240° SSW) is a generically plausible Arabian Sea SW-monsoon swell window but is not independently confirmed for this exact site in any source read this pass.
materials: Non-woven geotextile sand-filled containers ('Geotubes'/bags), built in ~30 m-long units [R1][R10]. R2 (Geosynthetics Magazine) discusses Kovalam only as an example of geotextile-bag failure ("debris strikes (Kovalam)") and does not itself state the 30 m unit length -- removed from this citation on re-verification (2026-09-25).

open_issues: No engineering drawing, GPS as-built survey, or dimensioned figure for the Kovalam reef was found in this pass (ours or Gemini's) — all footprint numbers here (ours and Gemini's) are estimates of varying rigor, not sourced as-built dimensions.

Gemini's two cited sources for crest depth/dimensions ('Kerala Harbour Engineering Dept Project Report 2011', 'Thomas et al. 2012') could not be located; they may be fabricated, badly mis-cited, or simply inaccessible online — flagged, not resolved.

(2011) 'Multi-Purpose Reefs – A Decade of Application' is very likely the actual technical source behind Raised Water Research's uncredited 'Mead and Borrero (2011)' reference and may contain real Kovalam performance/dimension data, but it sits behind ResearchGate/eCoast gates (eCoast requires an email-gated download) and could not be read this pass.

The 12 m tube/crest-width assumption used in our area estimate is not sourced for Kovalam specifically — borrowed by analogy from other ASR Ltd geobag reefs and from Gemini's own (also unsourced) assumption.

The 'Kovalam-Outline.jpg' hand-traced line could represent either the structure's crest outline or simply the visible foam/break-line pattern at one moment of one swell — sources do not label which, so its use here as shape evidence carries residual uncertainty.

Re-verification pass (2026-09-25) also opened three more images already hosted on the already-cited R1 page but not previously catalogued -- Kovalam-Geomat.jpg (a construction-beach photo of a large woven/mesh fabric sheet being hauled ashore with orange floats, headland visible offshore) and Kovalam-Reef-Underwater1.jpg / -Underwater2.jpg (close-range underwater shots of a smooth rounded mound with small fish, no scale reference) -- plus Gemini's own three cited photos (kovalam-reef-india.jpg, _gallery1.jpg, _gallery2.jpg). The volume/cross-section arithmetic checks out independently: 4800 m3 / 55 m2 assumed cross-section = 87.3 m of total tube length = 2.9 (~3) x 30 m units -- confirmed by recomputation. However, the claimed photographic corroboration ("S2 aerial photo shows ~4 visible dark parallel/sub-parallel submerged rows") is an overstatement: the PDF's aerial photo was downloaded and zoomed to high resolution (kovalam_page0_hires.png, 400 dpi) and at most 2 clearly discernible darker elongated submerged bands are visible (one with whitewater breaking along its seaward edge); the rest of the water shows diffuse texture that image compression and surface glare make impossible to confidently subdivide into 3 or 4 distinct bands. Wording corrected in the derivation table; the '3 units' conclusion itself is retained because it is primarily supported by the (disclosed, analogy-based) volume arithmetic, not by the photo count.
Recomputed independently with python/shapely from the stored polygon_m vertices: bbox x-span = 87.89 m, rounds to 87.9 m. Exact match.
Recomputed independently: bbox y-span = 41.61 m, rounds to 41.6 m. Exact match.

shapely.geometry.Polygon(polygon_m).area = 1083.31 m2 (vs. the stated 1083.5 m2, a 0.02% difference attributable to the stored vertices being rounded to 2 decimals rather than the original unrounded buffered-union polygon). Sanity cross-check: 3 tube segments x 30 m x 12 m = 1080 m2 (a flat-rectangle approximation) is consistent with the actual buffered/mitred-join polygon area of ~1083 m2. is_valid=True, exterior.is_simple=True, first vertex==last vertex (closed) -- all independently confirmed.

Recomputed independently: the true maximum pairwise vertex-to-vertex distance within the actual (non-rectangular) polygon is 92.05 m (between vertices [-43.1, 34.31] and [39.01, 75.92]), not 97.4 m. The stated 97.4 m turns out to be the diagonal of the bounding BOX (sqrt(87.9^2 + 41.6^2) = 97.2-97.4 depending on rounding) -- a quantity the polygon's own vertices never actually reach, since the bbox's far corners are empty space outside the fan shape. Checked the convention used by sibling verified/researched footprint files (e.g. opunake, southern-ocean-surf-reef-albany, borth): max_dimension_m in every other file is the true max pairwise vertex distance of the actual polygon (<= bbox diagonal), never the bbox diagonal itself. Corrected to 92.1 m for consistency and accuracy.

verification.item: Shape typology: chevron / echelon fan (not smooth crescent)
verification.evidence: S3 (Kovalam-Outline.jpg) re-downloaded and viewed directly (2026-09-25): the hand-traced line is unambiguously a stepped zigzag polyline with at least 4 straight segments meeting at 3 sharp-angle vertices -- a staircase pattern, not a smooth curve. This is strong, clear, independently-viewed evidence for a staggered/chevron structure. S2 (ASR aerial photo) independently re-viewed at high resolution: shows a single elongated, gently-curved-to-irregular dark submerged patch with whitewater along its leading edge and at least 2 discernible darker bands (see 'number of chained units' item above) -- weaker support than originally claimed for '4 parallel rows fanning from the headland,' but still consistent with a non-smooth, multi-part structure rather than one continuous uniform crescent arc. Overall chevron/fan-over-crescent verdict CONFIRMED, resting primarily on S3, with S2 as weaker corroboration than the original draft implied.

R1, R2, R10, S1, S2 re-checked/re-fetched: none states a crest or submergence depth for Kovalam. Targeted web searches for Gemini's two cited sources ("Kerala Harbour Engineering Dept Project Report 2011", "Thomas et al. 2012 Performance Assessment of Kovalam Multipurpose Reef") returned no matching document under either title. A real 2015 paper by Ng, Thomas, Phillips et al. ("Multifunctional artificial reefs for small islands", Ocean & Coastal Management) does exist and does include a real author named Thomas -- a plausible source of the citation confusion -- but its title, year, and subject (small islands, not Kovalam-specific) do not match Gemini's citation, and it was not accessible to confirm or deny a Kovalam depth figure. Default-to-unsupported correctly applied; value remains null.
